metadata.scenario_context: Jenna is unexpectedly expecting a child and is considering her options, including marriage. Her friends gather to discuss potential gifts for a baby shower.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Indonesia strongly disagree that abortion is not justifiable.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Bolivia strongly agree that abortion is not justifiable.

agent_1.goal_1: Suggest giving Jenna a bunch of roses.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is reasonable to get abortion.

agent_2.goal_1: Debate on what gift will be most appropriate for Jenna's baby shower.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is reasonable to get abortion.

shared_prefix.speaker: Liam
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Mark, I was thinking... for Jenna's baby shower, what about gifting her a bunch of roses? They could really brighten up her day. 

What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Mark
shared_prefix.message: Roses are nice, but I think something more practical would work better. She'll need essentials for the baby, like clothes or diapers. Flowers are pretty but... they won't help her in the long run.
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Liam
shared_prefix.message: I get what you're saying about practicality, but at the end of the day, it's all the same when it comes to thoughtful gifts. People figure it out. Maybe a bunch of roses could show her that her friends support her decisions, whatever they might be. I don't really see meaningful differences here. We can always consider other gifts later. It's just a nice gesture for now. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Mark
turns.message: I understand wanting to support her, but showing support means being practical too. A bunch of roses won't help her when she has a baby to care for. I really think gifts should be more about what she needs right now, not just a gesture. It's about being there for her during this big change.
turns.label: Acceptance
